reelection.rule: Rule: end of the current class term in legislators-current.yaml. Class 3 ends 2029-01-03. The November before that January 3 end is November 2028. The file does not store the election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 Senate votes, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 31. Nay or No: 9. Not Voting: 0. votes.question: H.R. 6500, as amended
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: The Senate passed H.R. 6500 as a continuing resolution that funds federal agencies into fiscal year 2027 and extends several expiring programs. A Yea passes that stopgap. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: Motion to Table Budd Amdt. No. 6747
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: An amendment would have deleted section 2019 of the stopgap, which until December 11, 2026 narrows which Agricultural Marketing Act products are covered by changes in Public Law 119-37. This vote was to table that deletion. A Yea kills the deletion and keeps section 2019; a Nay would have left it pending.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Collins Amdt. No. 6732 to H.R. 6500
votes.result: Cloture Motion Agreed to (91-6, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This vote would end debate on a substitute that replaces H.R. 6500's Africa-trade text with a stopgap funding the government into fiscal year 2027 and extending several programs. A Yea limits debate on that substitute. A Nay keeps debate open.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to H.R. 6500
votes.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Agreed to (89-4, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on starting consideration of H.R. 6500 as it then stood: an extension of duty-free treatment for certain African imports and of customs user fees. A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up that bill. A Nay blocks ending debate.

votes.question: S.Con.Res. 33, As Amended
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution establishes the congressional budget for the federal government for FY2026, sets forth budgetary levels for FY2027-FY2035, and provides reconciliation instructions for legislation that increases the deficit. A Yea agrees to it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Schiff Amdt. No. 5333
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: The sponsor's official statement of purpose for this amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 reads: “To establish a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to requiring the obligation of amounts appropriated to the Federal Emergency Management Agency to carry out the public assistance and hazard mitigation programs.” A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Wyden Amdt. No. 5336
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: The sponsor's official statement of purpose for this amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 reads: “To establish a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to requiring the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a study related to economic consequences of private or confidential drug pricing agreements struck by any Federal department, agency, or office with any pharmaceutical manufacturer.” A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Merkley Amdt. No. 5235
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: The sponsor's official statement of purpose for this amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 reads: “To establish a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to the impacts of hedge fund ownership of single-family homes and rent prices.” A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Paul Amdt. No. 5378
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: The sponsor's official statement of purpose for this amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 reads: “To reduce new budget authority for functions 150, 250, 500, and 600 in order to offset $70,000,000,000 of new spending by cutting $45,000,000,000 of foreign aid, eliminating $5,000,000,000 in refugee spending, cutting $16,000,000,000 from the Department of Education, and cutting $4,000,000,000 of National Science Foundation funding.” A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Motion to Waive All Applicable Budgetary Discipline Re: Markey Amdt. No. 5001
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: This vote was on waiving budget rules so an amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 could be considered. The sponsor's official statement of purpose for the amendment: “To create a point of order against legislation that would not decrease home electricity bills.” Waiving needs 60 votes (three-fifths). A Yea supports the waiver; a Nay keeps the budget point of order in place, which blocks the amendment.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.
financial_disclosures.note: Senate financial disclosures are filed through efd.senate.gov, a different system from the House Clerk index used here. Senate filings are not listed yet.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
